arte.universo: Slough, near London, England, in 1800: an astronomer's Georgian brick house and garden workshop with a big wooden telescope outside, wooden tables, small pieces of colored glass, a glass prism, old mercury thermometers with blackened bulbs, sunlight through tall windows and candles at night; then a modern Mexican teenager's living room today. No portraits and no recognizable real people: the astronomer is never shown, only his objects and places. Anonymous people only from behind or far away. No readable writing, letters or digits anywhere.

escena.accion: In a dark modern Mexican living room at night, the Pasita points a TV remote control at a television; a faint, almost invisible lime-green beam of light comes out of the tip of the remote
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, seen from behind and slightly to the side, small school backpack, arm stretched holding the remote
escena.objeto: A plain black TV remote with a soft lime-green glow at its tip and a faint beam (no labels or buttons with text)
escena.foreground: The arm of a sofa and a cushion, slightly blurred
escena.background: A dark television on a low cabinet, a window with distant city lights
escena.iluminacion: Very dark room, cold blue light from the window, the soft lime glow of the beam
escena.composicion: Medium-wide shot; the upper 42% is the dark, quiet wall and ceiling for the title

cuerpo: Con vidrios de color. Unos **calentaban más**.

escena.accion: In an English garden in 1800, next to a big old wooden telescope on a wooden frame, the Pasita holds up a small piece of red glass and a piece of green glass against the low sun, comparing them
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-right, three-quarter view from behind, small backpack, holding the two colored glasses up
escena.objeto: Small pieces of red, green and blue glass on a wooden table beside the telescope
escena.foreground: Grass and the edge of the wooden table, slightly blurred
escena.midground: The Pasita and the colored glass
escena.background: The large wooden telescope, a Georgian brick house, a pale evening sky
escena.iluminacion: Low golden late-afternoon sun, colored light passing through the glass pieces
escena.emocion: Curiosity: a small detail that does not fit
escena.composicion: Wide shot; the upper 42% is a dark, calm dusk sky for the title

cuerpo: Separó la luz del Sol **con un prisma**.

escena.accion: In a dark 1800 room, a single beam of sunlight enters through a gap in heavy shutters and passes through a glass prism on a wooden table, spreading a bright rainbow across the tabletop; the Pasita watches, amazed
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, three-quarter view, small backpack, leaning toward the rainbow
escena.objeto: A triangular glass prism and a vivid rainbow band from violet to red on the wooden table
escena.foreground: The edge of the table, slightly blurred
escena.background: Dark wood-panelled room, a thin line of sunlight from the shutters
escena.iluminacion: Almost total darkness except the sunbeam and the colors of the rainbow
escena.composicion: Medium shot; the upper 42% is the dark room above the beam

cuerpo: Del violeta al rojo, **subía la temperatura**.

escena.accion: Close view of the rainbow on the wooden table: three old glass mercury thermometers with black-painted bulbs lie side by side, each bulb resting in a different color of the rainbow; the Pasita kneels and looks closely at them
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-right, close, small backpack, eyes on the thermometers, focused
escena.objeto: Three old thin glass thermometers with blackened bulbs in the violet, green and red bands (scales illegible, no numbers)
escena.midground: The thermometers in the colored light
escena.iluminacion: The rainbow light on the table, everything else dark
escena.composicion: Close-medium shot from slightly above; the upper 42% is dark

escena.accion: On the dark wooden table, just beyond the red end of the rainbow, a single old thermometer lies in a dark area where no color is visible; a very faint lime-green glow surrounds its blackened bulb; the Pasita points at it, surprised
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, small backpack, pointing at the lone thermometer, mouth open
escena.objeto: One old thermometer with a blackened bulb in the dark beyond the red band, softly outlined in lime green (no numbers)
escena.foreground: The red edge of the rainbow, slightly blurred
escena.midground: The lone thermometer and the Pasita's hand
escena.iluminacion: Dim red light at the edge of the rainbow, darkness, a faint lime glow
escena.emocion: Surprise: something is there in the dark
escena.composicion: Medium close-up; the upper 42% is dark

cuerpo: Y en las cámaras que **ven de noche**.

post:
Tu control remoto usa una luz que no puedes ver. 📺

En 1800, el astrónomo William Herschel (el mismo que descubrió Urano) miraba el Sol con vidrios de colores y notó que unos calentaban más que otros. Separó la luz con un prisma y puso termómetros en cada color: del violeta al rojo, la temperatura subía.

Luego puso uno más allá del rojo, donde no se veía nada… y marcó todavía más calor. Había descubierto el infrarrojo, la primera luz invisible que conocimos.

Hoy está en tu control remoto, en las cámaras de visión nocturna y en los termómetros sin contacto. ¿Qué más usas que funcione con luz que no ves? 👇
